questions.question: Explain the role of a bank as a financial intermediary and how it makes a profit.
questions.expected_answer: A bank is a go-between: it accepts deposits from savers and lends them to borrowers (households, businesses, government). It pays savers interest at a lower rate and charges borrowers interest at a higher rate; the difference, plus fees for services, covers its costs and bad debts and leaves a profit.

questions.question: Name four services offered by banks.
questions.expected_answer: Any four: transactional accounts; savings accounts; fixed/notice deposits; home loans (bonds); vehicle finance; personal and business loans; overdrafts; credit and debit cards; EFTs, debit and stop orders; cellphone/app banking; foreign exchange; safe custody; merchant/card machine services; insurance and investments.

questions.question: Distinguish between interest earned and interest paid, and give two ways to reduce bank charges.
questions.expected_answer: Interest earned: paid by the bank to the customer on savings/deposits. Interest paid: charged by the bank (or lender) to the customer on loans and credit. Reduce charges (any two): choose a suitable account; use digital banking and card payments; draw cash at own bank's ATM or at a till point; avoid bounced debit orders; check fee guides and statements.
